name: Nest Doorbell wired 2nd gen (US)

radios.note: Google's install page connects it to Wi-Fi through the Google Home app. No Google page seen states the bands for this model; press and retailer listings say 2.4 and 5 GHz.

matter.note: No Google page states Matter for this model, and no CSA listing for it surfaced in search. A German news site reports Nest cameras and 'the Nest Doorbell' listed by the CSA for Matter 1.5.1 without firmware yet, but it does not name the model.

apple_home.note: No Google or Apple page found that lists this doorbell in Apple Home.

google_home.note: Set up in the Google Home app. Doorbell visitor announcements play on Google speakers and displays in the same home.

alexa.note: Through the Google Nest skill in the Alexa app. Google names this model for doorbell-press announcements once Visitor announcements is on in Google Home, and live view works on Echo Show when you ask for it.

smartthings.note: No official Google or SmartThings page found for this model; only forum posts and a 2020 article about older Nest devices.

home_assistant.note: The official Google Nest integration uses Google's Device Access API, which costs US$5. Google's Device Access list includes Nest Doorbell (wired), added in February 2023, with WebRTC live view and clip preview.

hubRequired.note: Needs Wi-Fi, the Google Home app and a Google Account; no hub or bridge is mentioned.

localControl.note: Google does not state whether any control works without its cloud.

power.note: Google requires a transformer rated 16–24 V AC, 10–40 VA; some homes need a new one. Google also lists an optional indoor plug-in power adapter.

localStorage.note: Google says it can hold up to an hour of events in the doorbell if Wi-Fi drops, but no local or microSD storage option is stated.

subscription.value: Event video history beyond 3 hours (Google Home Premium)
subscription.note: Google's comparison page lists 3 hours of event video with no plan and up to 60 days of event history with Google Home Premium.

summary: Set up in the Google Home app, the Nest Doorbell (wired, 2nd gen) announces visitors on Google speakers and displays in the same home. Alexa works through the Google Nest skill, with doorbell-press announcements and live view on Echo Show, and Home Assistant gets it via the Google Nest integration. It needs existing 16 to 24 V AC doorbell wiring and no hub. Free use keeps 3 hours of event video; up to 60 days needs Google Home Premium.
caveats: Needs doorbell wiring and a transformer rated 16–24 V AC, 10–40 VA; some homes need a new transformer.
Video history beyond 3 hours needs a paid Google Home Premium plan.
Home Assistant access goes through Google's Device Access API, which costs US$5.
Apple Home support is not confirmed.
